claims.text: The Public Utility Commission of Texas has proposed a new rule numbered 16 TAC Section 25.521 relating to Large Load Demand Management Service.
claims.quote: The Public Utility Commission of Texas (commission) proposes new §25.521 relating to Large Load Demand Management Service.
claims.source_title: Texas Register, August 14th, 2026, Proposed Rules, 16 TAC Economic Regulation

claims.text: Comments on the proposed rule must be filed by September 4th, 2026.
claims.quote: Comments must be filed by September 4, 2026.
claims.source_title: Texas Register, August 14th, 2026, Proposed Rules, 16 TAC Economic Regulation

claims.text: The commission directs that every comment refer to Project Number 58482.
claims.quote: All comments should refer to Project Number 58482.
claims.source_title: Texas Register, August 14th, 2026, Proposed Rules, 16 TAC Economic Regulation

claims.text: The proposal states that interested persons may file comments electronically through the interchange on the commission's website.
claims.quote: Interested persons may file comments electronically through the interchange on the commission's website
claims.source_title: Texas Register, August 14th, 2026, Proposed Rules, 16 TAC Economic Regulation

claims.text: The proposed rule would require ERCOT to develop a Large Load Demand Management Service to competitively procure demand reductions from large load customers.
claims.quote: ERCOT must develop a Large Load Demand Management Service (LLDMS) to competitively procure demand reductions from large load customers consistent with this section.
claims.source_title: Texas Register, August 14th, 2026, Proposed Rules, 16 TAC Economic Regulation

claims.text: The proposed rule defines a large load customer as an entity with a total non-coincident peak demand at a single site equal to or greater than 75 megawatts.
claims.quote: An entity with a total non-coincident peak demand at a single site that is equal to or greater than 75 megawatts (MW).
claims.source_title: Texas Register, August 14th, 2026, Proposed Rules, 16 TAC Economic Regulation

claims.method: case insensitive regex over the full text of the fetched page, counted in code and re-counted at ship. An absence is only a claim when the document it is absent from is named and the search that failed to find it is stated.

rejected.finding: Jennifer Carrig and Helen Bryant are individual Texans, residents, or ordinary members of the public rather than utilities
rejected.reason: The filing index publishes a party name, a file stamp, an item type and a description. It publishes nothing about who a filer is, where they live, or what they represent. The only defensible statement is what the party field literally shows.

rejected.finding: The rule that governs demand management for large electric loads is the category that covers data centers
rejected.reason: The proposed rule text as published in the August 14th, 2026 Texas Register does not contain the phrase data center anywhere, confirmed at zero occurrences on an independent fetch. The rule defines a large load customer by a 75 MW single site peak demand threshold. The docket's link to data centers is that the Data Center Coalition filed in it, not that the rule names them.

rejected.finding: The item type codes COM and PC expand to Comments and Public Comment
rejected.reason: No authoritative expansion was reachable. puc.texas.gov returned 503 and 402 to the checker. The codes appear only as the literal strings COM and PC and must not be expanded on a slide.

rejected.finding: Item 34 is the most recent filing in the docket
rejected.reason: The page proves it is the last of 34 rows under an ascending sort on a single result page. Most recent as of now is an inference about the live docket that a cached artifact cannot support.

rejected.finding: PFP expands to Proposal for Publication and OPDM to Office of Policy and Docket Management
rejected.reason: Both are plausible and neither is stated in any page reached this run. The abbreviations stay unexpanded.
